transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-02
- Time: 15:00 UTC (45 minutes scheduled)
- Duration: ~48 minutes (recording stopped at end)
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Aisha (CSM); Rachid, Sofia, Evan, Marta (Lantana)

Summary:
Quick implementation standup focused on encryption/KMS handoff, VPC peering and pilot performance plan. Confirmed stakeholders and next steps for SOC2 artifacts and SSO workflow. Agreed pilot timeline and owners; flagged one open legal question around data retention for embeddings.

Topics:
- KMS integration and key rotation policy
- VPC peering / private deployment network diagram
- Pilot scope and perf benchmark (tokens per second, 95th perc latency SLO)
- SSO/SAML setup and RBAC mapping
- Data retention / embeddings lifecycle and legal ask

Action items (captured in metadata): see action_items above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick off, quick roll call?
[00:10] Rachid: yeah hey, this is rachid, i'm head of m l ops at lantana, and i'll be owning the pilot.
[00:15] Sofia: sofia here, security lead, i'll be the compliance owner.
[00:18] Evan: evan platform eng, i'll do the networking work.
[00:22] Priya: priya from redwood, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll run the bench and the runtime config.
[00:27] Aisha: aisha from success, i'll track milestones.

[01:05] Jordan: cool, agenda — encryption and kms handoff, vpc peering, pilot scope and timeline, any blockers. wanted to surface the doc links first — shared deck and network diagram in the notes: https://redwood.app/s/lan-tana-kickoff-deck and a quick runbook here: https://redwood.app/s/lan-tana-runbook (note: ephemeral links).

[02:10] Rachid: quick background — we want to replace our in-house microservice for chat summarization with your hosted offering for the pilot. main constraints: latency under 350ms p95 for 1k QPS burst, and encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys.

[03:05] Priya: okay got it. latency target is reasonable if we tune batching and use a dedicated instance. for kms we support both cloud KMS and BYOK via customer-managed keys; can you confirm which provider you're using?

[03:26] Sofia: we use Aws K M S under central security. keys are rotated monthly via our key-ops team. we need rotation to be visible in redwood audit logs and we need a key usage policy that prevents export.

[04:10] Priya: that's fine, we can integrate with your k m s via our dedicated private deployment or via the VPC peering flow for dedicated customers. audit logs will include key-use entries, but i'll double-check the retention period in the docs.

[05:02] Evan: on the V P C side, we prefer peering rather than public egress. we'll want an architecture diagram with subnets and ingress rules. do you support private endpoints and no public internet access?

[05:20] Jordan: yes, private endpoints supported, you can opt for a private deployment in your VPC or our private offering — with VPC peering or transit. we also have an on-prem package if necessary. i'll upload the sample vpc diagram after the call.

[06:18] Marta: legal is asking about data residency for embeddings we store for retrieval — are embeddings considered customer data and what's the retention default?

[06:45] Aisha: quick note, we flagged data retention earlier, it might be in the S L A and the security packet. sofia, can you capture the retention requirement?

[07:05] Sofia: yes we need 90 days retention with ability to purge on request, and we require proof of deletion for compliance.

[08:10] Priya: for the pilot we can set TTLs for embedding store and provide a purge API, and we can confirm procedures to export deletion logs to your SIEM. will include that in the runbook.

[09:00] Jordan: moving to pilot scope — recommend 2-week pilot with synthetic and production-like traffic. initial traffic profile: 5k daily calls, burst to 1k QPS for 10 mins, target p95 <350ms. priya will propose batching and quantization profile.

[10:05] Priya: for that profile i'd suggest dedicated capacity with 2 GPU workers and aggressive batching for small inputs; we'll also try a quantized model variant for cost. i'll produce expected cost delta and latency estimates in the runbook.

[11:30] Evan: can we run a warmup to populate the KV cache? our workload is prefix heavy so cold-start will kill latency.

[12:05] Priya: yes, we'll include cache priming steps in the pilot playbook — sequence lengths, tokenization, and key patterns to prefill. for the run we'll provide a script to replay requests.

[13:40] Rachid: on observability — what telemetry do we get? token-level cost, per-route latency, traces? we need per-team dashboards.

[14:05] Jordan: Redwood Console gives per-route latency, token breakdown, tracing hooks and error analysis; we can set a dashboard and grant read-only views for your dashboards team via SSO. we'll map RBAC.

[15:02] Sofia: about SSO — we use saml 2.0 with role mappings. do you support SCIM for user provisioning?

[15:22] Priya: yes, SAML + SCIM supported. we'll need the IdP metadata file; i can share the SSO runbook with attribute mapping examples.

[16:30] Marta: who signs into the redwood console during pilot? security needs admin contacts logged.

[16:50] Jordan: Jordan and aisha will be admins; you'll have a separate security role. we'll document initial users in the onboarding checklist.

[18:05] Sofia: legal question — embeddings retention again, plus are logs encrypted at rest and in transit?

[18:30] Priya: logs are encrypted in transit and at rest; we support your KMS for encryption-at-rest. i'll attach the encryption whitepaper.

[19:45] Rachid: one technical deep dive — do you support local quantization on GPUs and how does that affect accuracy on our summarization tasks?

[20:05] Priya: we have quantization profiles per model; most summarization tasks are robust to 8-bit/4-bit quant, but we'll run a regression eval on a small prompt set. priya: note — minor misrecognition, "pria" meant "Priya".

[22:00] Jordan: Ok let's talk timeline: share vpc diagram + kms details by friday 2026-09-04, security to confirm SOC 2 doc by 2026-09-07, pilot runbook and batching config by 2026-09-06, benchmark run week of 2026-09-13. agree?

[23:25] Evan: yes that works. i'll start the peering request template and open a ticket with our netops.

[24:10] Sofia: i'll send the KMS policy and rotation schedule. also need to see proof of SOC2 type II report — where can we fetch that?

[25:05] Jordan: i'll drop a secure link to the compliance pack in the notes, and i'll mark it for sofia and legal.

[26:40] Marta: also want to define success criteria for the pilot — we want p95 <350ms, error rate <0.5% and cost per 1k tokens under threshold — will confirm exact numbers.

[27:05] Aisha: noted. success criteria doc to be shared and we'll capture in the pilot sign-off.

[28:30] Rachid: one more — data residency, our EU customers must keep embeddings in eu-west-1 region. is that possible?

[29:00] Priya: yes region pinning supported for hosted/dedicated deployments; for private VPC we can ensure the runtime is in eu-west-1. will note network egress restrictions.

[30:20] Jordan: small commercial / procurement note — if you go dedicated there will be a reserved capacity commit; we'll get legal and procurement engaged after pilot.

[31:10] Sofia: procurement will need a draft quote and an outline of potential overage fees.

[31:45] Jordan: ok procurement — we'll share a ballpark pilot quote and a dedicated capacity estimate if pilot scales.

[33:00] Priya: technical note — we'll run a short internal regression to validate model outputs on your sample prompts, but we recommend you run an eval with your judgment set to check for quality regressions. we'll help with an eval harness.

[34:20] Evan: for test dataset — i'll drop a sanitized subset into the shared folder and give privs.

[35:05] Rachid: regarding rollback and fallback — if the dedicated nodes get overloaded do you have automatic fallback to hosted model? we need graceful degradation.

[35:35] Priya: yes policy-based routing — we can fallback to a compatible model family with higher latency but still functional. we'll include fallback thresholds in the runbook.

[36:50] Jordan: any blockers from your side?
[37:00] Sofia: only coordination with key-ops and legal; otherwise ok.
[37:20] Evan: same, netops will need the diagram.

[38:10] Jordan: final recap: i'll share vpc diagram and compliance pack by 2026-09-04, priya will post the pilot runbook 2026-09-06, sofia to send KMS policy 2026-09-07, evan to confirm test dataset 2026-09-09. schedule pilot bench week of 2026-09-13.

[39:20] Marta: perfect — also can you add a quick note about ops escalation path? we'll need on-call contacts.

[40:00] Aisha: i'll add escalation matrix to the runbook and link it.

[41:35] Jordan: quick live Q/A — sofia asked about audit logs retention, default is 90 days but we can arrange longer retention as an add-on, we'll provide options.

[42:30] Priya: small tech followup — i'll include KV cache priming script and a sample replay workload (link will be in the runbook).

[44:00] Rachid: sounds good. last question — any known compatibility quirks with our current on-prem redis cache?

[44:25] Priya: none specific; we will test when we run the replay. if needed we can instrument the runtime to read from your cache topology.

[45:10] Jordan: ok thanks everyone, i'll send meeting notes and links right after. next sync in two weeks unless we need to accelerate for procurement.

[45:30] Sofia: thanks all.
[45:33] Evan: thanks.
[45:35] Jordan: bye.

References and shared artifacts:
- Runbook (draft): https://redwood.app/s/lan-tana-runbook
- Sample VPC diagram (to be uploaded): will appear in notes after call
- Encryption whitepaper and SOC2 pack: secure link sent via crm

End of transcript.
